arxiv-2307-16435.title: Magneto-optical Kerr and Faraday effects in bilayer antiferromagnetic insulators
arxiv-2307-16435.creator: Wan-Qing Zhu, Wen-Yu Shan
arxiv-2307-16435.description: Abstract Control and detection of antiferromagnetic topological materials are challenging since the total magnetization vanishes. Here we investigate the magneto-optical Kerr and Faraday effects in bilayer antiferromagnetic insulator MnBi 2 Te 4 . We find that by breaking the combined mirror symmetries with either perpendicular electric field or external magnetic moment, Kerr and Faraday effects occur.

arxiv-2505-19953.creator: Ondřej Straka, Jindřich Duník, Pau Closas, Tales Imbiriba
arxiv-2505-19953.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ondřej Straka, Jindřich Duník, Pau Closas, Tales Imbiriba. State-space estimation and tracking rely on accurate dynamical models to perform well. However, obtaining an accurate dynamical model for complex scenarios or adapting to changes in the system poses challenges to the estimation process. Recently, augmented physics-based models (APBMs) appear as an appealing strategy to cope with these challenges where the composition of a small and adaptive neural network with known physics-based models (PBM) is learned on the fly following an augmented state-space estimation approach.

arxiv-2507-00939.creator: Zepeng Wang, Juan Peypouquet
arxiv-2507-00939.description: Abstract We analyze the convergence rate of the monotone accelerated proximal gradient method, which can be used to solve structured convex composite optimization problems. A linear convergence rate is established when the smooth part of the objective function is strongly convex, without knowledge of the strong convexity parameter. This is the fastest convergence rate known for this algorithm.

pmc-10746185.description: Bacterial cell size is a multifactorial trait that is influenced by variables including nutritional availability and the timing of cell division. Prior work revealed a negative correlation between concentration of the alarmone (p)ppGpp (ppGpp) and cell length in Escherichia coli, suggesting that ppGpp may promote assembly of the division machinery (divisome) and cytokinesis in this organism.

pmc-11481715.creator: Ting Liao, Xiaoying Tian, Tianrong Huang, Yihong Wu, Xinxia Yu, Simeng Song

pmc-11644361.creator: Claudia Beatrice Bagnato, Antonella Bianco, Caterina Bonfiglio, Isabella Franco, Nicola Verrelli, Nicola Carella, Endrit Shahini, Marianna Zappimbulso, Vito Giannuzzi, Pasqua Letizia Pesole, Anna Ancona, Gianluigi Giannelli, Domingo J Ramos-Campo
pmc-11644361.description: Background: Steatotic liver disease associated with metabolic dysfunction (MASLD) affects up to about 30% of the general adult population and is closely related to obesity and the metabolic syndrome. Cortisol, a stress-related hormone contributing to hepatic fat accumulation and insulin resistance, also promotes progression of the disease.

pmc-11653916.description: Africa, with 18.3% of the world’s population, faces a significant research output gap, contributing only 2% of global research despite bearing a substantial disease burden. pmc-12360723.title: The Effectiveness of an App-Based Fitness Program on Self-Perceived Physical Functioning in Older Adults: Randomized Waitlist-Controlled Trial
pmc-12360723.creator: Siegfried Eisenberg, Birgit Trukeschitz
pmc-12360723.description: BackgroundA decline in physical functioning can result in a loss of independence, particularly in older adults. Information and communications technologies supporting physical activity, such as fitness apps, are perceived as promising tools to increase activity levels. However, only little is known about fitness apps’ impact on older people’s abilities and skills to accomplish activities of daily living.

pmc-12465831.title: RfeA from Streptococcus suis serotype 2 triggers NLRP3/Caspase-1-dependent pyroptosis leading to blood–brain barrier disruption
pmc-12465831.creator: Shuai Gao, Wentao Wu, Xingxing Xiao, Jun Li, Sheng Lei, Luying Wang, Xu Han, Yongliang Lou
pmc-12465831.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Streptococcus suis serotype 2 (SS2) is a prominent pathogen that impacts swine and presents a zoonotic threat to humans; it is a cause of bacterial meningitis, a severe condition linked to neurological impairment and elevated mortality rates. For SS2 to access the central nervous system, it must traverse the blood–brain barrier (BBB); however, the precise mechanisms underlying this process remain incompletely elucidated.

pmc-12552632.title: Large transient assemblies of Apaf1 constitute the apoptosome in cells
pmc-12552632.creator: Alicia C Borgeaud, Iva Ganeva, Calvin Klein, Amandine Stooss, Daniela Ross-Kaschitza, Liyang Wu, Joel S Riley, Stephen W G Tait, Thomas Lemmin, Thomas Kaufmann, Wanda Kukulski
pmc-12552632.description: Upon cell death signals, the apoptotic protease-activating factor Apaf1 and cytochrome c interact to form the apoptosome complex. The apoptosome is crucial for mitochondrial apoptosis, as it activates caspases that dismantle the cell. However, the in vivo assembly mechanism and appearance of the apoptosome remain unclear.

pmc-12838042.description: Structural valve deterioration (SVD) remains a key limitation in bioprosthetic heart valve (BHV) usage influenced by patient age.
